text.p: The semiconductor units of Siemens AG and Motorola Inc planned to build a 2.5 billion mark chip plant in Germany, business monthly Manager Magazin said on Wednesday.

The plant would cut production costs 30 percent by producing chips on silicon wafers measuring 300 millimetres instead of on the 200-millimetre wafers used today, the magazine reported in an article due to appear on May 16.
Manager Magazin said the plant, with 1,500 employees, would be located outside Dresden, in east Germany.
Siemens semiconductor spokesman Georg-Ludwig Radke told Reuters Siemens had no plans with Motorola for a production site in east Germany.
Asked if they had plans for a site in west Germany, Radke said, "We don't have further comment on this subject."
Siemens and Motorola are already working together on a plant in Virginia.
The government of the German state of Saxony has offered incentives to attract chip makers to Dresden. Like Siemens, Advanced Micro Devices Inc is also building a plant in the region.
